subject: Post-call recap: prompt outputs, residency & retention — next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Lenora Ghosh <lenora.ghosh@mednova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: prompt outputs, residency & retention — next steps

Lenora — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and the action items we agreed on so we have a single reference: 

What we covered (summary):
- Hosted default: prompt inputs + outputs are transient by default; we persist minimal telemetry for 24 hours to support debugging and fraud detection (no raw output dumps).
- Dedicated/Private: for customers that require custody, we offer options to store prompt outputs in customer-controlled storage (S3/GCS) with configurable TTL and region pinning.
- Redaction: we can enable PII redaction at inference time for sensitive fields (configurable per-route).
- Audit evidence: we can share SOC 2 report and our product logs schema for security review; we also produce per-request metadata (hashes/timestamps) rather than full plaintext unless requested on Private deployments.

Agreed next steps: 
1) I will send a short tech note and a MAP (mutual action plan) draft capturing the retention TTLs and choices (attached).
2) Lenora to confirm which data elements in your prompts you consider PHI/PII so we can map redaction rules.
3) If MedNova needs output persistence in-region, we will scope Dedicated vs Private and provide cost / timeline estimates.

Attachments: redwood-prompt-data-matrix.pdf (summary of what we store and why)

If that aligns, I can have Ben follow up with a short technical note that lists the default telemetry fields and what we anonymize.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0132

From: Lenora Ghosh <lenora.ghosh@mednova.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-01T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: prompt outputs, residency & retention — next steps

Kimberly — thanks for the clear summary. A couple clarifying questions before we move the MAP forward: 

- When you say "transient by default", do you mean raw prompt + full generated output are never persisted to disk in hosted mode? We need to be explicit for our internal risk committee.
- For the 24-hour telemetry: what specific fields are retained (IP, timestamp, model id, token counts?) and are those fields reversible to recreate the prompt/output?
- Encryption: is hosted storage encrypted with customer-specific keys (KMS) or platform-managed keys?
- Subprocessors & flow: can we get a list of subprocessors involved in logs/telemetry handling?

We will also share a short list of example prompt payloads that contain identifiers so you can propose redaction rules.

Lenora Ghosh
Security Lead — MedNova Health
lenora.ghosh@mednova.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Lenora Ghosh <lenora.ghosh@mednova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-01T18:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: prompt outputs, residency & retention — next steps

Lenora — great questions, answered inline below. Short version: hosted is designed to minimize retention of raw outputs; we can provide stronger controls for Dedicated/Private. 

- Raw prompt + output in hosted mode: not persisted as long-term storage. Short-lived artifacts may be held in service memory for the request lifecycle and in ephemeral logs; we do not keep full plaintext outputs beyond the transient window unless flagged for debugging by a customer or a legal hold.
- 24-hour telemetry fields: timestamp, model id, request id, token counts, anonymized route identifier, status code, and a request hash (SHA256) — the hash cannot be reversed to retrieve the prompt/output. We do not store user identifiers in plaintext in the telemetry by default; IPs can be redacted on request.
- Encryption: hosted storage is encrypted at rest with platform-managed KMS by default. For Dedicated/Private, we support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM integrations.
- Subprocessors: I'll attach our subprocessors summary and SOC2 pack in the follow-up (Ben will add the tech note).

Next step: Ben — can you add the technical breakdown (fields, retention window, anonymization rules) and attach the tech note so Lenora's team can review with their risk folks?

Thanks — Kimberly

> Kimberly — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and the action items we agreed on so we have a single reference:

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lenora Ghosh <lenora.ghosh@mednova.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-11-02T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: prompt outputs, residency & retention — next steps (technical note)

Hi Lenora — adding the promised technical detail for your security review. High-level points below; attached is a one-page tech note.

- Hosted (default):
  * Raw prompt + generated output: handled in-memory and surfaced to the caller; not written to persistent long-term storage.
  * Short-term telemetry (retention default = 24 hours): request_id, timestamp, model_name, token_counts, status_code, route_hash. No plaintext prompt or output is stored in telemetry. Request hash = SHA256(prompt || salt) — not reversible.
  * Debug captures: only captured if the customer toggles "debug capture" for a session; captures are encrypted and TTL-limited. We require explicit customer consent to enable capture.

- Dedicated/Private deployment options:
  * Customer-controlled persistence: outputs can be routed to customer S3 in a pinned region. TTL configurable (24h/7d/30d/90d/custom).
  * CMK support: customer managed keys available for encryption at rest.
  * Audit logs: full request/response logs available on Private deployments for incident investigation; access is role-based and auditable.

- PII handling & redaction:
  * We support per-route redaction rules (regex or structured field mapping) to remove or mask specified identifiers before any persistence.
  * For your sample payloads we recommend enabling the redaction preprocessor for MRN, SSN, and email addresses.

Attachments: tech-data-handling-note.txt (technical breakdown), MAP-draft-mednova.docx (mutual action plan draft)

If helpful, we can run a short proof-of-concept next week: deploy a small Private instance with in-region storage and a 30-day TTL so your risk team can validate controls.

—Ben
